result.stdout:
IdentityFlow Playwright agent auth cache

Usage:
  identityflow-auth-cache list --cache <path>
  identityflow-auth-cache clear --cache <path> [--user <user>] [--origin <origin>]
  identityflow-auth-cache totp add --cache <path> --origin <origin> --user <user> (--otpauth <uri> | --otpauth-stdin | --secret <base32> | --secret-stdin) [--account <name>]
  identityflow-auth-cache totp current --cache <path> --origin <origin> --user <user> [--account <name>] [--wait-fresh <seconds>]
  identityflow-auth-cache passkeys list --cache <path>

The CLI reads and writes unprotected cache files: secrets are stored as plaintext JSON guarded only by a 0600 file mode. Caches written with a cache protector must be managed by the test harness that owns the protector.
Prefer --otpauth-stdin or --secret-stdin so TOTP secrets do not appear in shell history or process listings.
Passkey browser login requires the IdentityFlow.Tooling.Playwright library so a test can attach a Chromium virtual authenticator to its Playwright IPage.
